1.title: 'God save king Solomon!'
1.text: Solomon was anointed with the oil from the tabernacle, to the sound of the trumpet, and the people shouted: 'God save king Solomon!' — confirming David's succession.

1.question: How is David described at the start of 1 Kings?
options: Old and failing in strength
Young and full of great strength
Sick and without any heir at all
Strong and leading the battles

1.question: Who exalted himself, declaring himself king without his father's knowledge?
options: Adonijah, David's son
Absalom, David's son
Joab, the army general
Shimei, David's servant

1.question: Who warned David of Adonijah's attempt to seize the throne?
options: The prophet Nathan and Bath-sheba
The priest Zadok and the general Benaiah
The general Joab and the priest Abiathar
The servants Shimei and Rei

1.question: What had David sworn to Bath-sheba about the successor?
options: That Solomon would reign after him
That Absalom would inherit the royal throne
That the kingdom would be divided among his sons
That Joab would be the next king

1.question: Whom did David have anointed king in his place?
options: Solomon
Adonijah
Nathan
Benaiah

1.question: Where was Solomon anointed king?
options: At Gihon, by Zadok and Nathan
At Hebron, by Joab and Abiathar
In the tabernacle, by Zadok and Shimei
In Jerusalem, by Nathan

1.question: How did the people react to Solomon's anointing?
options: They rejoiced with great celebration
They gathered together to mourn the choice
They split into two rival factions
They received the news with fear

1.question: What happened to Adonijah's guests when they heard about Solomon?
options: They were afraid and scattered
They attacked Solomon's servants in fury
They acclaimed Adonijah as king at once
They fled to Joab's tents

1.question: What did Adonijah do in fear of Solomon?
options: He caught hold of the horns of the altar
He fled in great haste to the house of Joab
He hid himself away in the tent of Abiathar
He ran quickly to the king's own palace

1.question: What did Solomon do with Adonijah at that moment?
options: He spared him, on condition he be faithful
He ordered him held until a new royal order
He gave him half the kingdom as part of the pact
He demanded he leave the city forever

1.question: What did Solomon say to Adonijah in sparing him?
options: To go home, if he would show himself a worthy man
To stay imprisoned until David decided his fate
To rule together with him on that same throne
To depart soon for distant foreign lands

2.title: David's last charge
2.text: Before dying, David charged Solomon: 'be thou strong, and show thyself a man; keep the charge of the Lord' — leaving him a spiritual legacy, not just a political one.

2.question: What central charge did David give Solomon before dying?
options: To keep the commandments of the Lord and be strong
To conquer all the neighboring nations around Israel
To raise heavy taxes upon all the people of Israel
To divide the kingdom among all his brothers

2.question: What did David charge Solomon concerning Joab and Shimei?
options: To deal justly with them
To make full peace with them
To appoint them to the priesthood
To reward them with lands

2.question: How did David end his days?
options: He died in peace and was buried in the city of David
He was deposed by his son and died in exile in a foreign land
He abdicated the throne in favor of Solomon and withdrew to the desert
He died in battle against the fierce Ammonites

2.question: What did Adonijah ask for, which cost him his life?
options: Abishag, David's servant, as wife
Half the kingdom and command of the army
The high priesthood and authority over the temple
The crown and throne of his father David

2.question: What did Solomon do to Adonijah over that request?
options: He had him killed, seeing in it a threat to the throne
He pardoned him and gave him a place of honor at court
He crowned him as governor over a far distant province
He exiled him forever from the land of Israel

2.question: What did Solomon do to the priest Abiathar?
options: He deposed him and banished him to Anathoth
He killed him for his loyalty to Prince Adonijah
He promoted him to high priest in Jerusalem
He ignored him and let him remain there

2.question: How did Joab die?
options: He was killed by the altar, by Solomon's order
In battle against the Philistines at the northern border
Of old age, surrounded by his sons and many grandsons
In exile, far from the city of Jerusalem

2.question: Who replaced Joab over the army?
options: Benaiah
Abiathar
Zadok
Adonijah

2.question: What condition did Solomon impose on Shimei?
options: That he not leave Jerusalem, on pain of death
That he pay an annual tribute to Solomon's house
That he serve permanently in the temple at Jerusalem
That he go into exile in a distant land

2.question: What happened to Shimei when he disobeyed and left Jerusalem?
options: He was executed
He was pardoned
He was promoted
He was exiled

3.title: The request that pleased God
3.text: Solomon could have asked for riches or long life, but he asked for 'an understanding heart to judge the people' — so God gave him also what he did not ask.

3.question: How did Solomon's reign begin in his relationship with God?
options: He loved the Lord, but still sacrificed in the high places
He worshiped many foreign idols brought in by his foreign wives
He completely rejected the temple and followed many pagan customs
He completely ignored the Law of Moses given to Israel

3.question: What did God offer Solomon in a dream at Gibeon?
options: To ask whatever he wished
An army that could never be defeated
Eternal life for his whole family
A visible sign in the sky

3.question: What did Solomon ask of God?
options: Wisdom to govern and discern good and evil
Gold and silver in great abundance for his treasury
A long life and many years of peaceful reign
Complete victory over all his enemies

3.question: What did God give Solomon, besides what he asked?
options: Also riches and honor
A son
A finished temple
Rule over Egypt

3.question: How did Solomon reveal his wisdom in the case of the two women?
options: He proposed dividing the baby, revealing the true mother
He cast lots before all the people who were gathered there
He consulted a prophet before carefully deciding the case
He arrested both women until he found the truth

4.title: 'Every man under his vine'
4.text: At the height of Solomon's peace, it was said every Israelite lived secure 'under his vine and under his fig tree' — a biblical image of prosperity and peace.

4.question: What does chapter 4 list at the start?
options: Solomon's chief officials
The tribes that rebelled
Battles fought by David
The priestly temple laws

4.question: How did Solomon arrange provision for the court?
options: Twelve deputies, each providing one month a year
By taxing heavy annual tribute from the neighboring Philistines
By importing grain and oil from Egypt for the royal palace
By appointing a single treasurer over the whole nation

4.question: What was life like in Judah and Israel under Solomon?
options: Prosperous and secure, 'every man under his vine'
In constant war with the neighboring kingdoms around
Under severe famine and scarcity throughout the land
In exile and oppression under foreign nations

4.question: What gift marked Solomon's reign?
options: An immense wisdom, given by God
A military strength feared by all neighboring nations
A wealth inherited directly from his father David
An alliance formed with Egypt

4.question: How does the Bible measure Solomon's wisdom?
options: Greater than that of all the wise men of the East
Equal to the wisdom shown by King David
Limited only to the affairs of the royal court
Restricted only to his proverbs

4.question: What did Solomon produce, showing his wisdom?
options: Thousands of proverbs and songs
A vast military and political empire
A new code of laws for the whole kingdom
Countless riches in gold and silver

4.question: Who came to hear Solomon's wisdom?
options: People of all nations and kings of the earth
Only the priests and Levites of the temple
Only the elders of the twelve tribes of Israel
No one besides the royal family itself

5.title: Why it fell to Solomon
5.text: David could not build the temple, having shed much blood in war; in a time of peace, it fell to his son Solomon to raise the house of the Lord.

5.question: With whom did Solomon make an alliance to obtain timber for the temple?
options: Hiram, king of Tyre
Pharaoh of Egypt
The king of Syria
The Philistines

5.question: What did Hiram supply for building the temple?
options: Cedars and cypress from Lebanon
Gold and silver brought from Egypt
Precious stones brought from Arabia
Soldiers for the royal guard

5.question: What did Solomon give Hiram in exchange for the timber?
options: Wheat and oil for his household
Half of the cities of Jerusalem
Gold taken from the temple treasury
Slaves captured in war

5.question: How did Solomon gather a workforce for the great work?
options: He levied thousands of laborers
He hired skilled Egyptian craftsmen for the project
He relied solely on members of the royal family
He waited for volunteers to come forward

6.title: A temple raised in silence
6.text: No sound of hammer, axe or tool was heard at the temple during construction: the stones were prepared offsite — a sign of reverence in raising the house of God.

6.question: When did Solomon begin to build the temple?
options: In the fourth year of his reign
In the seventh year of reign
Shortly after David's death
In the month of Ethanim

6.question: What was notable about the stones during construction?
options: They were prepared offsite; no hammer was heard at the temple
They were cut with iron axes inside the temple itself
They were carved with Egyptian symbols before being sent
They were polished with oil and pure wine before being set

6.question: What promise did God make Solomon about the temple?
options: He would dwell with Israel if he kept His commandments
That his descendants would reign forever over Israel
That the temple would be greater than his father David's house
That enemies would never cross his borders

6.question: With what was the interior of the temple lined?
options: Cedar and gold
Silver and bronze
Marble
Cloth

6.question: What was in the inner sanctuary (the Holy of Holies)?
options: Two wooden cherubim overlaid with gold
Twelve bronze pillars supporting the sanctuary's roof
A stone altar with horns on its four corners
A silver table for the bread of the presence

6.question: What were the temple's walls and doors like?
options: Carved with cherubim, palm trees and flowers, and overlaid with gold
Plain and covered only with polished bronze, without any carving
Painted purple and adorned with colorful precious stones
Made of solid stone without any carved adornment

6.question: How long did building the temple take?
options: Seven years
Forty years
One year
Twenty years

7.title: Jachin and Boaz
7.text: The two bronze pillars of the porch had meaningful names: Jachin ('he establishes') and Boaz ('in him is strength') — a reminder that the house rested on God.

7.question: What did Solomon build, besides the temple?
options: His own palace, over thirteen years
A fortified wall surrounding the city of Jerusalem
A large fleet of ships for trade with other nations
A second capital city for the kingdom

7.question: Who was Hiram, called from Tyre for the work?
options: A craftsman skilled in bronze
A military commander from Tyre
A consecrated priest of the temple in Tyre
A prophet sent by the Lord

7.question: What were the names of the two bronze pillars of the temple porch?
options: Jachin and Boaz
Aaron and Levi
Gad and Asher
Cain and Abel

7.question: What great bronze piece did Hiram make, resting on twelve oxen?
options: The molten 'sea' (a great basin)
A great throne of ivory covered in gold
A golden altar for the offerings
A large statue of cast bronze

7.question: What was the bronze 'sea' for in the temple?
options: For the priests to wash
For grain offerings
To burn the incense
To store rainwater

7.question: What other bronze pieces were made for the temple?
options: Ten bases with lavers (basins)
Twelve bronze altars for burnt offerings
Four bronze thrones for the princes
A single golden lampstand

7.question: Of what material were the temple's sacred vessels?
options: Of gold
Of clay
Of iron
Of silver only

7.question: Who made all these metal works for the temple?
options: Hiram, the craftsman of Tyre
Solomon himself, in person
The Levites in charge of the temple
Hired Egyptian craftsmen

7.question: What did Solomon store when the work was finished?
options: The treasures David had dedicated
The idols captured from neighboring peoples
The weapons won in the army's battles
The tribute paid by all Egypt

7.question: What does chapter 7 describe in detail?
options: The building of the palace and the temple's furnishings
Solomon's many wars against several neighboring kingdoms
The division of the kingdom among the twelve tribes of Israel
The visit of the Queen of Sheba to Jerusalem

8.title: The glory that filled the temple
8.text: When the priests came out, a cloud filled the temple: the glory of the Lord was so intense they could not stand to minister. God had accepted the house.

8.question: What did the priests bring into the Holy of Holies at the dedication?
options: The ark of the covenant
David's throne
The conquered idols
Elijah's mantle

8.question: What was inside the ark?
options: The two stone tablets of Moses
The pot of manna and Aaron's flowering rod
The priestly garments of Aaron and his sons
The jewels brought from Egypt

8.question: What filled the temple when the priests came out?
options: A cloud — the glory of the Lord
A rain of fire falling from the heavens
A strong wind that put out the torches
The sound of many trumpets

8.question: What did Solomon recall as he blessed the people?
options: The promise made to David, now fulfilled
The covenant made with Abraham, now renewed
Moses' prophecy about the promised land
The great victory over the Philistines

8.question: What question did Solomon ask in his prayer?
options: 'Will God dwell on the earth?', for the heavens cannot contain Him
'Will the Lord accept this temple?', for the people are unworthy of it
'Who will guard this ark?', for the enemies covet it
'Will the Lord return to Israel?', even after their sin

8.question: What did Solomon ask about prayers made toward the temple?
options: That God hear them from heaven and forgive
That they be repeated seven times a day
That they be accompanied by mandatory fasting
That they be made only at night

8.question: What did Solomon ask for times of drought and famine?
options: That God hear and forgive the repentant people
That He send rain without the people repenting
That He multiply the people's flocks immediately
That He forgive without requiring repentance

8.question: For whom else did Solomon pray, besides Israel?
options: For the foreigner who would come to pray at the temple
For the children of Israel scattered among the nations
For the priests who served in the sanctuary
For the armies that went out to war

8.question: What did Solomon ask for when the people sinned and were carried captive?
options: That, repenting, God hear and forgive them
That they be freed without ever repenting
That a new king would soon come to free them
That they remain captive there forever

8.question: How did Solomon describe Israel before God in the prayer?
options: As an inheritance God brought out of Egypt
As a chosen nation among all the empires
As a strong people who subdued other nations
As a remnant scattered among the Gentiles

8.question: What did Solomon do when he finished the long prayer?
options: He blessed all the congregation of Israel
He offered a thousand sacrifices personally
He gathered the elders to renew the covenant
He consecrated new priests for the temple

8.question: What did Solomon ask the people's heart to be?
options: Wholly the Lord's, keeping His commandments
Set on riches and honor before all the nearby nations
Fearful of foreign kings more than of God Himself
Forgetful of the sins committed by their ancestors

8.question: How did the dedication of the temple end?
options: With many sacrifices and a great feast
With the people fasting before the ark for seven days
With the public reading of the tablets of Moses' law
With the king tearing his robes in a sign of humility

9.title: 'Mine eyes shall be there'
9.text: God said He had hallowed the temple and that 'mine eyes and mine heart shall be there perpetually' — but this depended on the faithfulness of Solomon and the people.

9.question: What did the Lord do after Solomon finished the temple?
options: He appeared to him again, accepting the house
He sent an angel to anoint him
He commanded him to rebuild the tabernacle
He warned him through the prophet Nathan

9.question: What warning did God give Solomon?
options: That if they turned to other gods, Israel and the temple would be destroyed
That if they forsook the law of Moses, they would lose all their wisdom
That if they multiplied horses, the kingdom would never have lasting peace
That his children would reign forever over all the nations

9.question: What did Solomon give Hiram, which displeased him?
options: Twenty cities in Galilee
One hundred talents of silver from the treasury
Ten cities in the region of Naphtali
Thirty talents of pure gold

9.question: How did Solomon carry out his great building projects?
options: With forced labor of non-Israelite peoples
With volunteers from all the tribes
With soldiers levied for the royal work
With riches brought from Ophir by ships

9.question: What did Solomon's fleet bring from Ophir?
options: A great quantity of gold
Large flocks of sheep and cattle
Fine garments and rare spices
Plenty of silver and pure bronze

10.title: The queen of the South
10.text: Jesus would cite 'the queen of the South,' who came from the ends of the earth to hear Solomon's wisdom, as an example of one who seeks truth wholeheartedly (Matthew 12).

10.question: Who came to test Solomon with hard questions?
options: The Queen of Sheba
Hiram of Tyre
A royal servant
The king's son

10.question: How did the Queen of Sheba react on seeing Solomon's wisdom and wealth?
options: She was overwhelmed: 'the half was not told me'
She was disappointed and said: 'it is not as they told me'
She doubted his words and demanded further proof
She praised only the buildings, without mentioning the king

10.question: What did the Queen of Sheba give Solomon?
options: Gold, spices and precious stones
Royal garments and chariots of war
Horses, chariots and chosen servants
Fertile lands south of Israel

10.question: What was Solomon's throne like?
options: Of ivory, overlaid with gold
Of polished bronze with inlays
Of carved cedar with jewels
Of solid, gleaming silver

10.question: What was silver like in Solomon's days, it was so abundant?
options: It was like stones, of little special value
It was worth less than the bronze used for utensils
It was kept only within the royal treasuries
Brought only from the mines of Ophir

11.title: Even the wise can fall
11.text: Solomon, the wisest man, turned away by compromising with the idolatry of his foreign wives — a warning that wisdom without faithfulness is not enough.

11.question: What turned Solomon's heart away in his old age?
options: His many foreign wives and their gods
The great wealth and horses he had gathered in Israel
The constant wars against the neighboring kings of Israel
The idolatry that David had practiced in his youth

11.question: What did Solomon go so far as to do, in turning away?
options: He built high places for pagan gods
He rebuilt the temple to worship Ashtoreth
He offered human sacrifices to Ammonite idols
He forbade the sacrifices to the Lord

11.question: What did the Lord decide because of Solomon's unfaithfulness?
options: To rend the kingdom, but only after his death
To forgive him completely and restore his wisdom
To destroy all his descendants during his lifetime
To send plagues upon the kingdom of Israel

11.question: For whose sake would God leave one tribe to Solomon's house?
options: For the sake of David and Jerusalem
For the sake of Solomon and his temple
For the sake of David's faithful servants
For the sake of the tribe of Judah

11.question: What adversaries did God raise up against Solomon?
options: Hadad the Edomite and Rezon
Hiram, king of Tyre, and his armies
The kings of Moab and Ammon united
Pharaoh and his army

11.question: What sign did the prophet Ahijah give Jeroboam?
options: He tore a garment into twelve pieces and gave him ten
He tore his own royal robe apart in front of King Solomon
He prophesied the building of a brand new temple in Israel
He anointed Jeroboam's head with sacred oil

11.question: What did Ahijah's prophecy mean?
options: That Jeroboam would reign over ten tribes of Israel
That Rehoboam would lose the whole kingdom at once
That Solomon would repent before his death
That the temple would soon be destroyed

11.question: What happened at the end of Solomon's reign?
options: He died and his son Rehoboam reigned in his place
He was deposed and Jeroboam took the whole throne
He lived forty more years in peace with Israel
He fled to Egypt with his servants

12.title: The 'sin of Jeroboam'
12.text: So the north wouldn't go up to Jerusalem, Jeroboam made two golden calves (at Beth-el and Dan). This idolatry, the 'sin of Jeroboam,' condemns king after king in the book.

12.question: Where did Rehoboam go to be made king?
options: To Shechem
To Jerusalem
To Hebron
To Beth-el

12.question: What did the people ask of Rehoboam?
options: To lighten Solomon's heavy yoke
To expel all of Solomon's counselors
To give them fertile lands in Israel
To abolish the temple taxes

12.question: What counsel did Rehoboam follow, angering the people?
options: The young men's, answering harshly
Jeroboam's, offering peace to the people
The priests', asking for more sacrifices
A general's counsel, urging war

12.question: What did Israel do in the face of Rehoboam's harshness?
options: It rebelled: 'To your tents, O Israel!'
It accepted paying heavier tributes
It sent elders to negotiate terms
It asked for a new pact of submission

12.question: How was the kingdom divided?
options: Ten tribes with Jeroboam; Judah and Benjamin with Rehoboam
Seven tribes with Jeroboam; the rest with Rehoboam and his sons
Twelve tribes were divided equally between the two rival kings
All the tribes still remained united under Rehoboam

12.question: What did Jeroboam do so the north would not worship in Jerusalem?
options: He made two golden calves, at Beth-el and Dan
He built his own altars in the northern cities
He sent messengers to negotiate with Rehoboam
He forbade the people from going up to the temple

12.question: What else did Jeroboam institute, leading the people astray?
options: His own priests and feasts, outside the Law
A temple greater than the one in Jerusalem
A new alliance with the king of Assyria
A royal guard to watch the borders

13.title: Obeying the word of God
13.text: The man of God performed mighty signs, yet died for disobeying a clear command of the Lord. The chapter teaches that neither gifts nor miracles replace obedience.

13.question: What did the man of God prophesy against at Beth-el?
options: Against Jeroboam's idolatrous altar
Against King Jeroboam and all his house
Against the false prophets of Baal in Beth-el
Against the whole city of Beth-el

13.question: What happened to Jeroboam's hand when he stretched it out against the prophet?
options: It dried up, then was restored
It became permanently paralyzed with no cure
It instantly turned into solid stone
It burst into flames instantly

13.question: What had the man of God been commanded not to do?
options: Not eat or drink there, nor return by the same way
Not enter the king's house nor accept any gift from him
Not prophesy against any other altar in the region
Not touch any sacred object in the temple

13.question: Who deceived the man of God into returning to eat?
options: An old prophet of Beth-el
A priest sent from Jerusalem
A messenger of King Jeroboam
One of the prophet's sons

13.question: What happened to the man of God for disobeying?
options: He was killed by a lion on the way
He was badly wounded by a bear on the road
He was captured by King Jeroboam's soldiers
He went blind for the rest of his life

13.question: What did the lion do that was unusual beside the body?
options: It stood by, not devouring the body or the donkey
It roared loudly all through the night by the road
It dragged the body deep into a nearby darker cave
It ran away as soon as it saw the travelers

13.question: What did Jeroboam do after this sign?
options: He did not turn from his evil way
He appointed more priests for the high places
He built another altar in a different city
He called the people to repent

14.title: The measure of the northern kings
14.text: From here on, nearly every king of Israel is judged by walking 'in the sin of Jeroboam' — the calf idolatry that split the worship of God.

14.question: Why did Jeroboam's wife go disguised to the prophet Ahijah?
options: To learn what would happen to their sick son
To ask the Lord to heal her sick child from illness
To bring gifts to the prophet before his death
To consult about the future of the kingdom

14.question: What did the blind Ahijah prophesy to Jeroboam's house?
options: That it would be destroyed because of its idolatry
That it would become the greatest military power
That it would reign over all neighboring nations
That it would become a model of righteousness

14.question: What would happen to Jeroboam's sick son?
options: He would die as soon as his mother entered the city
He would be raised as Jeroboam's successor to the throne
He would recover his health and reign after his father
He would be taken away to Egypt to hide there

14.question: What in fact happened to the son, fulfilling the prophecy?
options: He died when his mother arrived, and all Israel mourned him
He survived the illness and later became king over all Israel
He was secretly taken away to Egypt and hidden until adulthood
He was healed and all the people celebrated for seven days

14.question: What was Rehoboam's reign like in Judah?
options: He did evil, with high places and idols
He was righteous and faithful to God
He reigned without any wars
He walked in the ways of David

14.question: Who invaded Judah and plundered the temple in Rehoboam's time?
options: Shishak, king of Egypt
Ben-hadad, king of Syria
Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon
The invading Ammonites

14.question: What did Rehoboam make in place of the gold shields taken away?
options: Bronze shields
He rebuilt the temple
He asked Syria for help
He surrendered

15.title: Asa, a whole heart
15.text: Among so many wicked kings, Asa of Judah stands out: he removed the idols and his heart was 'perfect toward the Lord' all his life — a rare good example.

15.question: Who was Asa, king of Judah, in this chapter?
options: A king who did right and removed idols
A king who promoted idolatry throughout the kingdom
A weak king who submitted to the neighboring kings
A king who rebuilt the pagan high places

15.question: What was Asa's heart like toward the Lord?
options: Perfect (whole) all his days
Turned toward idols for most of the time
Faithful only during the early years of his reign
Always unstable and full of doubts

15.question: With whom did Asa make a league against Baasha of Israel?
options: With the king of Syria
With Egypt
With the Philistines
With Tyre

15.question: Who reigned in Israel after Jeroboam, doing evil?
options: Nadab, his son
Zimri's son
Elah's cousin
Ahab, brother

15.question: Who killed Nadab and destroyed Jeroboam's house?
options: Baasha
Zimri
Omri
Elisha

15.question: What did the destruction of Jeroboam's house fulfill?
options: The prophecy of Ahijah
A dream of Asa
The law of Moses
A request of the people

16.title: Ahab and Jezebel
16.text: Ahab was worse than all the kings before him: he married Jezebel, princess of Sidon, and established Baal worship in Israel — which will provoke Elijah's ministry.

16.question: What pattern recurs among the kings of Israel in this chapter?
options: They do evil, following the sin of Jeroboam
They govern with justice, fearing the Lord God
They rebuild the temple of the Lord in Jerusalem
They abandon idolatry and seek God

16.question: Who killed Elah and seized the throne for only seven days?
options: Zimri
Omri
Baasha
Ahab

16.question: What did Zimri do when he saw himself surrounded and lost?
options: He burned the palace down over himself
He fled into the desert with his servants
He surrendered peacefully to Omri's soldiers
He hid himself in the nearby mountains

16.question: Who became king and founded the city of Samaria?
options: Omri
Zimri
Ahab
Jehu

16.question: How does the chapter describe Ahab, son of Omri?
options: He did evil more than all the kings before him
He was the most righteous and God-fearing king of Israel
He restored pure worship in the temple at Jerusalem
He ruled Israel with wisdom and peace

16.question: Whom did Ahab marry, deepening the idolatry?
options: Jezebel, and he came to serve Baal
The daughter of the king of Sidon, to seal an alliance
A priestess of Baal brought from Tyre
A foreign idolatrous princess

16.question: What did Ahab build for Baal in Samaria?
options: A temple and an altar
A sanctuary for Ashtoreth
A watchtower on the city wall
A sacred golden statue

17.title: Elijah against Baal
17.text: The drought Elijah announced was a direct blow against Baal, worshiped as the god of rain and fertility: the Lord would show who really governs the sky and life.

17.question: What did Elijah announce to king Ahab?
options: That there would be no dew or rain except by his word
That the armies of Israel would be defeated by the Philistines
That the rain would come abundantly to bless the whole land
That Israel would be freed from the Philistines' yoke

17.question: How was Elijah fed by the brook Cherith?
options: By ravens, which brought him bread and meat
By women of the city, who brought him fruit and milk
By servants of king Ahab, hidden by the brook
By a compassionate widow from Sidon

17.question: What miracle happened at the house of the widow of Zarephath?
options: The meal and oil did not run out during the drought
The widow found a hidden treasure in her own house
The boy never felt any hunger while Elijah dwelt there
A spring of pure water gushed near the house

17.question: What happened to the son of the widow of Zarephath?
options: He fell sick and died
He went blind
He ran from home
He was healed soon

17.question: What did Elijah do for the widow's dead son?
options: He prayed, and the Lord raised him to life
He called the elders of the city to mourn with him
He offered a sacrifice over the boy's body
He took him to the town's physician

18.title: 'How long halt ye between two opinions?'
18.text: On Carmel, Elijah challenged the people: 'How long halt ye between two opinions? If the Lord be God, follow him; but if Baal, then him.' It was time to decide.

18.question: Whom did Elijah meet before Ahab, who had hidden prophets of the Lord?
options: Obadiah, Ahab's steward
Jehu, army captain
Ben-Hadad, Syrian king
Naaman, Syrian general

18.question: What did Ahab call Elijah when he met him?
options: 'The troubler of Israel'
'The greatest enemy of Israel'
'The adversary of my kingdom'
'A servant of the Lord'

18.question: What challenge did Elijah propose on Mount Carmel?
options: To see which God would answer by fire: the Lord or Baal
To see which altar would remain standing after the storm
To see how many prophets of Baal would convert to the Lord
To see who could endure longest without food

18.question: How many prophets of Baal did Elijah face alone?
options: Four hundred and fifty
Three hundred and sixty-five
Two hundred and fifty-three
Only a hundred prophets

18.question: What did the prophets of Baal do, in vain, to make their god answer?
options: They cried out and cut themselves, but there was no answer
They prayed in very deep silence throughout the whole morning
They built an altar much taller and much bigger than Elijah's
They offered gold and silver upon the altar of Baal

18.question: What did Elijah do to his altar before praying?
options: He soaked it with water three times
He covered it with pure gold and fine silver
He hid it behind several large stones
He burned it before the sacrifice

18.question: What happened when Elijah prayed to the Lord?
options: Fire fell from heaven and consumed everything
It rained abundantly at once over the whole land
The earth shook violently before all the people
Absolutely nothing happened right away

18.question: What did the people cry out when they saw the fire from heaven?
options: 'The Lord, he is God! The Lord, he is God!'
'Long live Baal, the god of thunder and rain!'
'Long live great King Ahab forever and ever!'
They all fell completely silent at once

18.question: What happened to the prophets of Baal after the challenge?
options: They were put to death
They fled
They were converted
They were imprisoned

18.question: What did Elijah announce after the challenge ended?
options: The return of the rain, after praying seven times
Another great drought lasting for many long years
The imminent and certain death of King Ahab himself
A new war against the whole kingdom of Syria

19.title: Seven thousand who had not bowed
19.text: Elijah thought he was alone, but God revealed there were 7,000 in Israel who had not bowed their knees to Baal — he was not alone in faithfulness.

19.question: What led Elijah to flee to the wilderness, discouraged?
options: Jezebel's threat to kill him
Fear of King Ahab's anger
His soldiers' betrayal
Exhaustion from the journey

19.question: How was Elijah sustained on the way to Horeb?
options: An angel fed him
Ravens served him
He found a feast
He fasted without food

19.question: Where was the Lord, and not in the wind, earthquake or fire?
options: In a still small voice
In a great distant thunderstorm
In a thick and dark cloud
In a revealing dream

19.question: Whom did Elijah call to be his successor, finding him plowing?
options: Elisha
Jehu
Hazael
Obadiah

20.title: God of hills and valleys
20.text: The Syrians said Israel's God was 'a god of the hills,' not of the valleys. God gave the victory in the valley precisely to show that he reigns over all.

20.question: Who besieged Samaria, demanding Ahab's surrender?
options: Ben-hadad, king of Syria
Tiglath-pileser, king of Assyria
Sennacherib, king of Assyria
Hazael, king of Syria

20.question: What did a prophet announce to Ahab about the battle?
options: That the Lord would deliver the Syrians into his hand
That the Syrians would prevail if Ahab did not repent
That Ahab must flee to the desert with his people
That Israel would be delivered to the Syrians

20.question: What was the result of the first clash with Syria?
options: Israel won
Israel lost
There was a truce
Samaria fell

20.question: What did the Syrians say about the God of Israel?
options: That he was 'a god of the hills,' not of the valleys
That he only had power over Israel's prophets
That he was a weak god, defeated by Baal's idols
That he had no power over war at all

20.question: What happened in the second battle, fought in the valley?
options: Israel won again, showing God's power
The Syrians retreated without fighting, fearing Israel's power
There was great slaughter on both sides, with no victor
Syria conquered part of the Israelite territory

20.question: What did Ahab do with Ben-hadad on defeating him?
options: He spared him and made a covenant
He captured him and exiled him forever
He executed him before the people
He made him his personal servant

20.question: What did a prophet do to rebuke Ahab?
options: He pretended to be wounded and led Ahab to judge himself
He disguised himself as a beggar and prophesied Ahab's fall
He called the elders and denounced Ahab publicly
He sent a sealed letter denouncing the king

20.question: What did the prophet announce to Ahab for sparing Ben-hadad?
options: That his life would answer for the king he had released
That his kingdom would be divided among his sons
That famine would ravage the land of Israel for seven years
That he would lose the throne to a Syrian general

21.title: Naboth's inheritance
21.text: Naboth refused to sell the vineyard because it was his fathers' inheritance, sacred under Israel's Law. For this Jezebel had him killed — a crime of greed and injustice.

21.question: What did Ahab covet from Naboth?
options: His vineyard, near the palace
His vineyard, near the city gate
His field of wheat, near the city
His large flock of sheep

21.question: Why did Naboth refuse to sell the vineyard to Ahab?
options: It was his fathers' inheritance
He had promised never to sell it to the king
He feared a curse from God on anyone selling land
He had already given it to the temple

21.question: What did Jezebel plot so Ahab could have the vineyard?
options: She falsely accused Naboth and had him stoned
She bribed the elders to declare him guilty of theft
She sent soldiers to drive him from his own vineyard
She offered the king another piece of land

21.question: What did Elijah say to Ahab about the crime?
options: 'Hast thou killed, and also taken possession?'
'Repent, and the Lord will forgive you completely'
'Thy house shall be exalted above all Israel forever'
'Keep my commandments and prosper always'

21.question: What judgment did Elijah announce on Ahab's house?
options: That it would be destroyed, and dogs would eat Jezebel
That his sons would rule over Israel for many generations
That he would be blessed with great riches and long life
That Naboth would be resurrected soon after

21.question: What happened when Ahab humbled himself before God?
options: God delayed the punishment to his son's days
God promised to fully restore his stolen vineyard
Elijah declared that Ahab would be crowned king forever
He was pardoned without any condition whatsoever

22.title: Micaiah, alone against 400
22.text: While 400 prophets flattered Ahab, only Micaiah dared to tell the uncomfortable truth — an example of faithfulness that cost dearly, but came to pass.

22.question: What did Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, propose to Ahab?
options: To ally to retake Ramoth-gilead
To pay tribute to Syria's king for peace
To divide the kingdom of Israel between them
To attack Egypt before facing Syria

22.question: What did Ahab's 400 prophets say about the battle?
options: To go up, for he would win
To avoid the battle for now
To seek help from the Arameans first
To wait for a sign from heaven

22.question: Whom did Jehoshaphat ask to consult, a prophet of the Lord?
options: Micaiah
Elijah
Elisha
Nathan

22.question: What did Micaiah truly prophesy?
options: Defeat: 'I saw all Israel scattered upon the hills'
Certain victory over Syria and the conquest of Ramoth-gilead
A long peace between Israel and Judah for many years to come
Jehoshaphat's death before entering the battle

22.question: How did Micaiah explain the false prophets?
options: A lying spirit in their mouths, to deceive Ahab
An angel of the Lord sent to confirm Ahab's victory
The wisdom of the elders revealed to them by the Lord
The king's fear, which made them agree with him

22.question: What did Ahab do with Micaiah over the prophecy?
options: He had him imprisoned
He had him whipped publicly
He had him exiled from the kingdom
He rebuked him harshly

22.question: What did Ahab do to try to escape the prophecy in battle?
options: He disguised himself as an ordinary soldier
He fled secretly to Samaria during the night
He surrendered to Syria's king before battle
He stayed hidden in his royal tent

22.question: How did Ahab die, despite the disguise?
options: A randomly shot arrow struck him
A Syrian soldier's sword pierced him in the chest
A stone hurled from the wall struck him down
He was badly wounded in his right leg

22.question: What happened to Ahab's blood, fulfilling the prophecy?
options: The dogs licked it
It was buried in gold
It vanished
It turned to dust

22.question: What was Jehoshaphat's reign like in Judah?
options: He walked in the right ways, like Asa his father
He made alliances with wicked kings and worshiped foreign idols
He allowed the people to freely worship idols
He reigned only a few months before dying

22.question: Who reigned in Israel after Ahab's death?
options: Ahaziah, his son, who did evil
Omri, his grandson, who rebuilt Samaria
Jehoram, his elder brother, who sought Baal
Elisha, the prophet, who healed the land
